_comment: compiler-bench on the cloud engines: databricks-enzyme + both fabric engines.
Purpose: debug the cloud adapters remotely. Their code paths need live credentials,
so they cannot be exercised on a dev box. Dispatch GCI with
experiments_file=src/containers/benchmark-server/experiments/compiler-bench-cloud.json
COST: limit is deliberately 25, not the full 2186-query corpus. Every Databricks
materialized view is backed by its own Lakeflow pipeline, so N queries means N
pipelines created and dropped. Raise the limit only once a small run is green.
EXPECTED FAILURES on the first run:
- fabric-openivm-jvm-35 / fabric-jvm-35 fail immediately and by design: the repo
drives Fabric through dbt-over-Livy and has no direct SQL statement client, so
the adapter raises instead of reporting zeros that would read as 'nothing
incrementalizable'. The fix is a Fabric equivalent of
spark_openivm_sources.LivyClient. See engines_cloud._FabricAdapter.
- databricks-enzyme is written against the real APIs (EXPLAIN CREATE MATERIALIZED
VIEW ... REFRESH POLICY INCREMENTAL STRICT for the up-front verdict, then a real
CREATE + REFRESH) but has never run against a live warehouse.
Artifacts to read afterwards:
mount/compiler-bench/results/<engine>/results.csv   per-query phase + classification
mount/compiler-bench/results/<engine>/summary.json  aggregate percentages
mount/compiler-bench/corpus/spark/translation.csv   which queries LPTS could express
